PO-7, new tonight. A fence claim must cover every path the session CAUSES to be written,
including a path that exists only inside a dispatch brief at the moment of claiming.
"Claim before you write" is read as "before YOUR hands write", and a session that writes
only through subagents can satisfy that reading while owning nothing.

PO-8, new tonight. When a writer agent is refused by the fence on files the orchestrator
legitimately owns (the M13 false miss, where a raw harness session id is compared
against a derived bm1- label), the answer is SANDBOX THEN INTEGRATE. Never an identity
override, never a forced write, never hand-editing STATE.md. Four lanes used it tonight
and all four integrated cleanly, and the orchestrator re-proving red then green in the
main checkout caught things the sandbox passes could not.

The gate recipe held again, and earned its keep on its first run: it caught a defect
that a passing 56-test suite could not see, because the defect lived in a different
suite's registry. Per-suite green is not gate green.

The load rule fired for real. At load average 143.90 with 1030 processes, a 68 second
suite took over 12 minutes. Read the load before a battery, and when the machine is
